s: Which one of the following correctly represents the standard west-to-east regional division of the Himalayas with their bounding rivers?
o: Punjab Himalaya—Indus to Sutlej; Kumaon Himalaya—Sutlej to Kali; Nepal Himalaya—Kali to Teesta; Assam Himalaya—Teesta to Dihang
Punjab Himalaya—Indus to Beas; Kumaon Himalaya—Beas to Kali; Nepal Himalaya—Kali to Teesta; Assam Himalaya—Teesta to Dihang
Punjab Himalaya—Jhelum to Sutlej; Kumaon Himalaya—Sutlej to Gandak; Nepal Himalaya—Gandak to Teesta; Assam Himalaya—Teesta to Lohit
Punjab Himalaya—Indus to Kali; Kumaon Himalaya—Kali to Teesta; Nepal Himalaya—Teesta to Dihang; Assam Himalaya—Dihang to Lohit
x: The standard Burrard boundaries are Indus–Sutlej, Sutlej–Kali, Kali–Teesta and Teesta–Dihang. The Punjab Himalaya is sometimes extended up to the Beas in some accounts, but Sutlej is the standard boundary.
tq: Start from the sure river pair and eliminate options that shift the regional boundaries.

s: The Punjab Himalaya is chiefly associated with which of the following groups of peaks?
x: Nanga Parbat, Rakaposhi and Haramosh are prominent peaks of the Punjab or Kashmir-Himachal Himalaya.
tq: Use the regional-division cluster to associate each division with its characteristic peaks.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Kumaon Himalaya — Sutlej to Kali — Nainital and Bhimtal
Nepal Himalaya — Indus to Sutlej — Everest and Kanchenjunga
Assam Himalaya — Kali to Teesta — Namcha Barwa
Punjab Himalaya — Teesta to Dihang — Nanga Parbat
x: The Kumaon Himalaya lies between the Sutlej and Kali and includes the lakes Nainital and Bhimtal. Everest and Kanchenjunga belong to the Nepal Himalayan sector, while Namcha Barwa marks the eastern end of the Assam Himalaya.
tq: Match the boundary rivers with the distinctive geographical features of the same division.

s: The Kumaon Himalaya is particularly associated with which of the following glaciers?
x: Pindari, Milam and Kafni glaciers are associated with the Kumaon Himalaya of Uttarakhand.
tq: Test a distinctive list through direct recall rather than confusing it with Trans-Himalayan glaciers.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the parallel ranges of the Himalayas:
1. The Karakoram is part of the Trans-Himalaya.
2. The Ladakh Range continues eastwards into Tibet as the Kailash Range.
3. The Zaskar Range lies south of the Karakoram and is separated from the Pir Panjal by the Kashmir Valley.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Karakoram and Zaskar are Trans-Himalayan ranges, Ladakh continues as Kailash in Tibet, and the Kashmir Valley separates Zaskar from Pir Panjal.
tq: Check each range by its position and continuation before selecting the coded combination.

s:
Arrange the following Himalayan ranges from north to south:
A. Himachal
B. Karakoram
C. Shiwalik
D. Himadri
E. Ladakh
x: From north to south, the sequence is Karakoram, Ladakh, Himadri, Himachal and Shiwalik.
tq: Fix the northernmost Trans-Himalayan range first, then move southward through the three principal Himalayan ranges.

s: Which one of the following statements about the Himadri is correct?
o: It is the youngest and narrowest Himalayan range.
It lies south of the Shiwalik and contains simple Jura-type folds.
It is the loftiest and oldest Himalayan range and has a granite core.
It has an average elevation of about 1,300 metres and consists mainly of river deposits.
x: The Himadri, or Greater Himalaya, is the loftiest and oldest Himalayan range, with an average elevation above 6,000 metres and a granite core.
tq: Use the contrast between the oldest, loftiest Himadri and the youngest, narrowest Shiwalik.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the Himachal or Lesser Himalaya?
o: Pir Panjal — Jhelum-Beas sector — approximately 300 km
x: Pir Panjal is a major range of the Himachal Himalaya extending for about 300 km in the Jhelum-Beas sector. Dhauladhar, Mussoorie and Mahabharat are also associated with the Lesser Himalaya.
tq: Pair the range with the correct parallel belt and approximate extent.

s: The Shiwalik Range is best described as a range that is
o: the loftiest range with an average elevation above 6,000 metres
a Trans-Himalayan range extending into Tibet
the oldest, widest and composed mainly of granite
the youngest and narrowest, with simple Jura-type folds of river deposits
x: The Shiwalik is the youngest and narrowest Himalayan range, about 15–50 km wide, with an average elevation of about 1,300 metres and simple folds formed from river deposits.
tq: Compare age, width, elevation and composition to distinguish the Shiwalik from the other ranges.

s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Trans-Himalaya?
o: It was formed after the main Himalayan ranges and contains the lowest plateau of India.
It was formed before the Himalayas, and the Ladakh Plateau is the highest plateau in India.
It lies south of the Himadri and is younger than the Shiwalik.
It consists only of the Shiwalik and Himachal ranges.
x: The Trans-Himalaya formed before the Himalayas. The Ladakh Plateau is regarded as the highest plateau in India.
tq: Use the age comparison and the distinctive superlative associated with the Ladakh Plateau.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Kashmir, Kangra and Kullu valleys lie in the Himachal or Lesser Himalaya. Kashmir Valley is not a valley of the Shiwalik Range.
tq: Find the one location assigned to the wrong parallel range.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
x: Patli Dun is located in Uttarakhand. Kotli Dun and Nalagarh Dun are associated with Himachal Pradesh, while Dehradun is in Uttarakhand.
tq: Use state-location matching to separate the similarly named Himalayan duns.

s: Karewas of the Kashmir Valley are best described as
o: marine sediments of the Tethys Sea used for rubber cultivation
glacial moraines of the Shiwalik Range used for jute cultivation
volcanic cones used for tea cultivation
lacustrine deposits of Pleistocene age used for saffron cultivation
x: Karewas are lake or lacustrine deposits in the Kashmir Valley. They are of Pleistocene age and are important for saffron cultivation.
tq: Identify the landform from its origin, age and characteristic agricultural use.

s: Which one of the following peaks is correctly matched with its range and location?
x: Kamet is a peak of the Himadri in the Kumaon or Garhwal Himalaya of Uttarakhand. Dhaulagiri is in Nepal, Namcha Barwa is in the Assam Himalaya of Tibet, and Kailash belongs to the Trans-Himalaya.
tq: Start with the peak whose range, regional division and country are all precisely aligned.

s: Which of the following statements regarding Kanchenjunga is correct?
o: It is wholly within Nepal and belongs to the Punjab Himalaya.
It marks the western end of the Assam Himalaya in Tibet.
It lies in the Himadri on the India-Nepal boundary and is the highest peak wholly in India.
It is located in the Karakoram under Pakistan-China control.
x: Kanchenjunga belongs to the Himadri and lies on the India-Nepal boundary. It is the highest peak wholly in India, although it is not entirely within India.
tq: Distinguish “highest peak wholly in India” from the highest peak associated with India’s claim.

s: Godwin Austen, commonly known as K2, is correctly described as
o: a peak of the Himadri, 8,586 metres high, wholly within Uttarakhand
a peak of the Nepal Himalaya, 8,611 metres high, wholly within Nepal
a peak of the Karakoram, 8,611 metres high, under Pakistan-China control and second highest in the world
a peak of the Assam Himalaya, 8,586 metres high, located in Tibet
x: Godwin Austen or K2 is 8,611 metres high and belongs to the Karakoram. It lies in territory under Pakistan-China control and is the world’s second-highest peak.
tq: Separate the peak’s height, range, political control and world ranking instead of relying on a single superlative.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nanga Parbat — eastern end of Assam Himalaya — China
Namcha Barwa — eastern end of Assam Himalaya — Tibet
Dhaulagiri — western end of Punjab Himalaya — Pakistan
x: Namcha Barwa marks the eastern end of the Assam Himalaya and is located in Tibet, China. Nanga Parbat marks the western end of the Himalayan arc in the Punjab Himalaya.
tq: Use the western-end/eastern-end contrast to eliminate the swapped peak-location pairs.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Nanda Devi — Himadri, Kumaon Himalaya — Uttarakhand
x: Nanda Devi is a peak of the Greater Himalaya in the Kumaon Himalaya and is located in Uttarakhand. Dhaulagiri is in the Nepal Himalaya.
tq: Check the peak against both its Himalayan division and its state or country.

s: The Himalayan arc extends approximately from Nanga Parbat to Namcha Barwa over a length of
x: The Himalayan arc extends for approximately 2,414 km from Nanga Parbat in the west to Namcha Barwa in the east.
tq: Choose the precise length rather than the rounded distractor values.

s: Which one of the following correctly represents the variation in the width of the Himalayas?
o: About 50 km in Kashmir and 1,000 km in Arunachal Pradesh
About 500 km in Kashmir and 200 km in Arunachal Pradesh
About 400 km throughout the entire Himalayan arc
About 200 km in Kashmir and 500 km in Arunachal Pradesh
x: The Himalayas are wider in Kashmir, where their width is about 500 km, and narrower in Arunachal Pradesh, where it is about 200 km.
tq: Watch for the reversed west-to-east comparison in the distractors.

s:
Consider the following statements about the structure of the Himalayas:
1. The folds of the Himadri are asymmetrical.
2. The steep slope of the Himalayas faces the plains.
3. The gentler slope faces Tibet.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The Himadri has asymmetrical folds; the Himalayan slope towards the plains is steeper, while the Tibetan side is gentler.
tq: Test the complete structural pattern and avoid reversing the two slopes.

s: The uplift of the Himalayas is associated with Tethys sediments and occurred mainly during the
o: Eocene to Pliocene period of the Tertiary
x: The Himalayas were uplifted from Tethys sediments during the Tertiary, broadly from the Eocene to the Pliocene, approximately 60 to 7 million years ago.
tq: Link the geological material, period and approximate time span in one sequence.

s: The collision responsible for the formation and continued uplift of the Himalayas occurred between the
x: The Indian Plate collided with the Eurasian Plate approximately 4–5 crore years ago. The Himalayas are still rising because tectonic convergence continues.
tq: Identify the two plates directly involved rather than selecting another major tectonic plate.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four major structural zones of the Himalayas?
x: The four structural zones are the Indus-Tsangpo Suture Zone, Main Central Thrust, Main Boundary Thrust and Himalayan Frontal Fault. Great Rift Valley Zone is not included in this classification.
tq: Recall the named structural list and identify the outside term.

s: The Himalayan range takes a sharp knee-bend near Namcha Barwa at the
x: The Himalaya makes a knee-bend at the Dihang gorge near Namcha Barwa and then turns southwards as the Purvanchal hills.
tq: Associate the distinctive geomorphic change in direction with its exact gorge and peak.
sec: Purvanchal hills and the Molasse basin

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Patkai Bum lies in Arunachal Pradesh along the Myanmar border. Naga Hills are in Nagaland, Manipur Hills in Manipur and Mizo Hills in Mizoram.
tq: Use state-hill matching and eliminate the systematic state swaps.
sec: Purvanchal hills and the Molasse basin

s: Which of the following statements about the Purvanchal hills is correct?
o: They extend from Kashmir to Himachal Pradesh without entering the North-East.
They are the southern continuation of the Himalayas after the Dihang knee-bend and generally range from 500 to 3,000 metres in height.
They are formed by a westward turn of the Himalayas at the Sutlej gorge.
They consist exclusively of the Shiwalik hills of Uttarakhand.
x: After the knee-bend near Namcha Barwa and the Dihang gorge, the Himalayas turn south as the Purvanchal hills. Their heights generally range from 500 to 3,000 metres.
tq: Apply the direction-change clue and the elevation range to identify the Purvanchal description.
sec: Purvanchal hills and the Molasse basin

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Barail Range — links Naga and Mizo hills — highest range of Assam
x: The Barail Range links the Naga and Mizo hills and is the highest range of Assam. Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills belong to Meghalaya and form part of the Shillong Plateau.
tq: Begin with the distinctive Barail description and reject options that interchange the North-Eastern states.
sec: Purvanchal hills and the Molasse basin

s: The Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills are associated with the
o: Ladakh Plateau of Jammu and Kashmir
x: Garo, Khasi and Jaintia are the principal hill groups associated with the Shillong Plateau in Meghalaya.
tq: Use the three-hill group as a distinctive geographical cluster.
sec: Purvanchal hills and the Molasse basin

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the alignment of the major Purvanchal hill groups?
o: Garo-Khasi-Jaintia run east-west, while the Mizo and Rakhine hills run north-south.
All the hill groups run exclusively west-east.
All the hill groups form a single east-west range without intersection.
Naga and Mizo hills run east-west, while Garo-Khasi-Jaintia run north-south.
x: The Garo-Khasi-Jaintia and Naga hills generally run east-west, joining the north-south Mizo and Rakhine hills. The specified contrast is correctly stated in option a.
tq: Compare the two directional alignments rather than treating all North-Eastern hills as one trend.
sec: Purvanchal hills and the Molasse basin

s: The Molasse Basin in the Indian Himalayan context is associated with
x: The Molasse Basin is associated with Mizoram and consists of soft, unconsolidated deposits.
tq: Pair the basin with its state and characteristic material.
sec: Purvanchal hills and the Molasse basin

s: How many broad groups are included under the classification of the northern mountains based on relief and alignment?
x: The northern mountains are classified into three broad groups: the Himalayas, the Trans-Himalayas and the Purvanchal.
tq: Distinguish the count of broad northern-mountain groups from the separate regional and structural counts.

s: Which one of the following correctly gives the three longitudinal parallel ranges of the Himalayas?
x: The three principal longitudinal parallel ranges are Himadri or Greater Himalaya, Himachal or Lesser Himalaya and Shiwalik or Outer Himalaya.
tq: Separate the longitudinal-range classification from the regional west-to-east classification.

s: The Himalayas are divided into how many broad regional divisions extending from west to east?
x: The four west-to-east regional divisions are Punjab, Kumaon, Nepal and Assam Himalaya.
tq: Use the named regional sequence to confirm the count rather than confusing it with the three parallel ranges.

s: Which one of the following represents the correct classification by the three principal bases mentioned for the northern mountain system?
o: Northern mountains—3; longitudinal parallel ranges—3; regional divisions—4; structural zones—4
Northern mountains—4; longitudinal parallel ranges—3; regional divisions—3; structural zones—5
Northern mountains—3; longitudinal parallel ranges—4; regional divisions—4; structural zones—3
Northern mountains—5; longitudinal parallel ranges—4; regional divisions—3; structural zones—4
x: The counts are three northern-mountain groups, three longitudinal parallel ranges, four regional divisions and four structural zones.
tq: Compare the four counts together and reject options that interchange the two threes and two fours.

s: Approximately what proportion of India's area is occupied by plains according to the stated relief-share classification?
x: Plains form the largest relief division of India and account for about 43 percent of the country’s area.
tq: Choose the precise approximate share and avoid shifting the stated percentage by ten points.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding Himalayan mountain passes:
1. Zoji La lies in the Zaskar sector of Ladakh and connects Srinagar with Leh.
2. Banihal Pass is located in the Pir Panjal Range and connects Jammu with Srinagar.
3. Shipki La is associated with the entry of the Sutlej into India and provides access towards Tibet.
4. Nathu La connects Gangtok with Tibet through the Chumbi Valley.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements are correct. Zoji La, Banihal, Shipki La and Nathu La have the stated locations and connecting routes.
tq: Use the pass–route association and check each statement independently.

s:
With reference to Himalayan passes, consider the following statements:
1. Rohtang Pass is located in Himachal Pradesh in the Pir Panjal Range and connects Kullu with Lahaul-Spiti.
2. Lipulekh Pass is located in Uttarakhand and forms part of the India-Nepal-China tri-junction route.
3. Bomdi La provides the route between Tawang and Lhasa.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Rohtang, Lipulekh and Bomdi La are associated with the respective regions and routes stated.
tq: Split the options by verifying the pass, state and route combination.

s: The heights of Banihal Pass and Rohtang Pass are approximately
x: Banihal Pass has an elevation of about 2,833 metres, whereas Rohtang Pass has an elevation of about 3,978 metres.
tq: Compare the numerical values directly and watch for reversal of the pair.

s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of avalanche-prone Himalayan passes?
o: Zoji La, Khardung La, Rohtang and Mana
Banihal, Shipki La, Nathu La and Bomdi La
Lipulekh, Banihal, Zoji La and Shipki La
Rohtang, Nathu La, Bomdi La and Lipulekh
x: Zoji La, Khardung La, Rohtang and Mana are identified as avalanche-prone passes.
tq: Identify the complete group rather than selecting a familiar individual pass.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nathu La — Gangtok-Tibet route through the Chumbi Valley
x: Nathu La connects Gangtok with Tibet through the Chumbi Valley. The other routes are associated with Zoji La, Shipki La and Banihal respectively.
tq: Start from the sure pass–route pair and eliminate the swapped connections.

s:
Consider the following statements about glaciers:
1. Siachen Glacier is situated in the Karakoram Range, in the Nubra region.
2. Siachen marks the northern limit of Ladakh.
3. Baltoro, Biafo and Hispar glaciers are located in Gilgit-Baltistan in the Karakoram region.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Siachen lies in the Karakoram's Nubra region and marks Ladakh's northern limit, while Baltoro, Biafo and Hispar are in the Karakoram sector of Gilgit-Baltistan.
tq: Group glaciers by their range and position before evaluating the statements.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Baltoro Glacier belongs to the Karakoram Range, not the Greater Himalaya. Gangotri is in the Greater Himalaya, while Pindari and Milam are associated with the Kumaon region.
tq: Find the single reversed glacier–range association.

s: Gangotri Glacier is associated with which one of the following combinations?
o: Pir Panjal Range and source of the Chenab
Kumaon Range and source of the Mandakini
Greater Himalaya and source of the Bhagirathi
x: Gangotri Glacier is located in the Greater Himalaya of Uttarakhand and is the source of the Bhagirathi at Gaumukh.
tq: Match the glacier with both its range and its associated river source.

s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Glacier)
a. Siachen
b. Baltoro
c. Gangotri
d. Pindari

List-II (Range or region)
i. Kumaon
 ii. Greater Himalaya
 iii. Karakoram, Nubra region
 iv. Karakoram, Gilgit-Baltistan
x: Siachen is in the Karakoram's Nubra region, Baltoro is in Karakoram in Gilgit-Baltistan, Gangotri belongs to the Greater Himalaya, and Pindari belongs to Kumaon.
tq: Start from the distinctive Siachen–Nubra and Gangotri–Greater Himalaya pairs.

s:
The Himalayas are significant to India because they
1. form India's northern boundary.
2. act as a climatic barrier.
3. have contributed debris that helped build the Indo-Gangetic Plain through the Shiwalik system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The Himalayas define India's northern boundary, act as a climatic barrier, and Shiwalik debris contributed to the formation of the Indo-Gangetic Plain.
tq: Treat geographical significance as a cause-and-effect set rather than as isolated facts.

s: Which one of the following correctly compares the Himadri and the Shiwalik ranges?
o: Himadri is the oldest and loftiest, whereas Shiwalik is the youngest and narrowest.
Himadri is the youngest and narrowest, whereas Shiwalik is the oldest and loftiest.
Both Himadri and Shiwalik are the oldest and loftiest ranges.
Both Himadri and Shiwalik are the youngest and narrowest ranges.
x: The Himadri is described as the oldest and loftiest Himalayan range, while the Shiwalik is the youngest and narrowest.
tq: Check both sides of the comparison; reversed adjectives form the main distractor.

s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the western and eastern ends of the Himalayas respectively?
x: Nanga Parbat marks the western end of the Himalayas, while Namcha Barwa marks their eastern end.
tq: Use the first–last method for geographical end-point questions.

s:
Assertion (A): The Shiwalik range has an important role in the formation of the Indo-Gangetic Plain.
Reason (R): The Shiwaliks consist largely of debris derived from the Himalayan ranges.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the debris carried and deposited from the Himalayan ranges explains the Shiwalik contribution to the Indo-Gangetic Plain.
tq: Test whether the reason explains the stated geographical effect, not merely whether both facts are true.
